structure: Part 1, the address lookup simulator. Read in full: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/stubs/federated/AddressLookupSimulatorController.java (163 lines: one GET route, a bearer check, a switch over reserved search terms, a three-addresses fixture and a no-results fixture), its test AddressLookupSimulatorControllerTest.java (194 lines, 14 tests), application.yml (the address-lookup-simulator block, lines 103 to 104, read with the whole file), application-local.yml (30 lines, no address-lookup override) and README.md's Federated-credential simulators section (lines 67 to 74). Covered: the route, the postcode and find parameters and their 400, the eight reserved terms (SW1A 1AA, ZZ1 1ZZ, QQ1 1QQ, XX1 1XX, YY1 1YY, TT1 1TT, Buckingham Palace, Downing Street) and what each answers, every field of the 3 fixture addresses, the default no-results answer, the bearer signature, audience and expiry check with its 401 body, the expected-audience default, and every test. Left to other parts: the STS and Entra simulators that issue the tokens.

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in trade-imports-ins-backend.
claims.quote: The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in `trade-imports-ins-backend`.

claims.statement: The address search takes two optional query parameters, postcode and find.
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find)

claims.statement: The simulator treats postcode and find identically: the same reserved terms give the same answers whichever parameter carries them.
claims.note: The comment says what find really matches (a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town) is a question only the real gateway can answer, and dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are given, the simulator searches on postcode and ignores find, because the term is postcode whenever postcode is present.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A search with neither postcode nor find answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".
The bearer token is checked before the search parameters, so a request with a bad token and no search term answers 401, not 400.
The search term SW1A 1AA answers 200 with JSON holding three addresses.
The three-addresses answer has a header whose totalResults is the string "3", and a results array.

The first fixture address is Buckingham Palace: addressLine "BUCKINGHAM PALACE, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", subBuildingName "BUCKINGHAM PALACE", buildingName, buildingNumber and street all null, town "LONDON", postcode "SW1A 1AA", country "ENGLAND", uprn "100023336901", match "1", matchDescription "EXACT", language "EN".
claims.quote: { "addressLine": "BUCKINGHAM PALACE, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", "subBuildingName": "BUCKINGHAM PALACE", "buildingName": null, "buildingNumber": null, "street": null, "town": "LONDON", "postcode": "SW1A 1AA", "country": "ENGLAND", "uprn": "100023336901", "match": "1", "matchDescription": "EXACT", "language": "EN" }
claims.note: The Javadoc says this is the case dev actually returned, where subBuildingName carries the whole name.

claims.statement: The second fixture address is 1 Downing Street: addressLine "1 DOWNING STREET, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", subBuildingName and buildingName null, buildingNumber "1", street "DOWNING STREET", town "LONDON", postcode "SW1A 1AA", country "ENGLAND", uprn "100023336902", match "1", matchDescription "EXACT", language "EN".
claims.quote: { "addressLine": "1 DOWNING STREET, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", "subBuildingName": null, "buildingName": null, "buildingNumber": "1", "street": "DOWNING STREET", "town": "LONDON", "postcode": "SW1A 1AA", "country": "ENGLAND", "uprn": "100023336902", "match": "1", "matchDescription": "EXACT", "language": "EN" }

claims.statement: The third fixture address is Unit 1, Downing House: addressLine "UNIT 1, DOWNING HOUSE, DOWNING STREET, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", subBuildingName "UNIT 1", buildingName "DOWNING HOUSE", buildingNumber null, street "DOWNING STREET", town "LONDON", postcode "SW1A 1AA", country "ENGLAND", uprn "100023336903", match "1", matchDescription "EXACT", language "EN".
claims.quote: { "addressLine": "UNIT 1, DOWNING HOUSE, DOWNING STREET, LONDON, SW1A 1AA", "subBuildingName": "UNIT 1", "buildingName": "DOWNING HOUSE", "buildingNumber": null, "street": "DOWNING STREET", "town": "LONDON", "postcode": "SW1A 1AA", "country": "ENGLAND", "uprn": "100023336903", "match": "1", "matchDescription": "EXACT", "language": "EN" }

claims.statement: All three fixture addresses share the postcode SW1A 1AA and the town LONDON.

The three fixture addresses are the three ways a name lands in the gateway's fields (whole name in subBuildingName; number and street; sub-building, building name and street), which is what makes composing address line 1 awkward.
claims.quote: The three results are the three ways a name lands, which is what makes composing address line 1 awkward

claims.statement: The fixture is shaped like the real dev gateway response of 2026-09-17, not the published v2.1 specification: everything upper case, country free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, match a string and counts as strings.
claims.quote: Shaped like the real dev response of 2026-09-17, not like the published v2.1 specification: everything upper case, {@code country} free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, {@code match} a string, and counts as strings.

claims.statement: The search term ZZ1 1ZZ answers 204 No Content with no body.
The search term QQ1 1QQ answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid".
Only the reserved term QQ1 1QQ triggers the invalid-postcode 400: the simulator does not check postcode format, so any other malformed postcode answers the no-results fixture.
claims.note: The switch has no format check; every term not listed falls to the default branch.

claims.statement: The search term XX1 1XX answers 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable".
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved throttled postcode.

claims.statement: The search term YY1 1YY answers 200 with an HTML body, not JSON: "<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>".
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved proxy-error postcode.

claims.statement: The search term TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds and then answers 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
claims.note: delayedOk calls Thread.sleep(15_000) then jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE). No test covers this term.

claims.statement: The free-text search terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" answer 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
The reserved free-text terms are fixtures for demonstrating find, not a model of what find matches: a result from the simulator says nothing about whether the same search returns results in dev.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Any search term that is not reserved answers 200 with a no-results JSON body: totalResults the string "0" and an empty results array.
Reserved terms match exactly and case-sensitively, so a partial term such as "Buckingham", a lower-case "sw1a 1aa" or a postcode without its space answers no results.
claims.note: A Java string switch is exact and case-sensitive, and the term is not trimmed or normalised. The "Buckingham" case is proven by addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved.

claims.statement: Every answer the simulator gives that is not 204 or the HTML proxy error is JSON.
The simulator checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would: signature, audience and expiry, before serving any fixture.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures

claims.statement: A request with no Authorization header, or one that does not start with "Bearer " (case-insensitive), answers 401.
A bearer that is not a parseable signed JWT answers 401.
A bearer whose RSA signature does not verify against the simulator's Entra signing key answers 401.
claims.note: So only a token issued by the stub's own Entra simulator is accepted.

claims.statement: A bearer whose audience is missing or does not contain the expected audience answers 401, and the simulator logs a warning naming the audience it rejected.
claims.quote: log.warn("Address lookup simulator rejected a bearer with audience {}", claims.getAudience());

claims.statement: A bearer with no expiry time, or one whose expiry has passed, answers 401.
claims.quote:
if (claims.getExpirationTime() == null || claims.getExpirationTime().before(new Date())) {
            return unauthorized();

claims.statement: Every 401 answers the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway's validate-jwt policy returned in dev on 2026-09-17.
claims.quote: { \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }

claims.statement: A 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The expected audience is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, from ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, defaulting to api://33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333.
The expected audience must match the Scope that ins-backend requests once /.default is stripped, api:// prefix included; the dev gateway rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.
claims.quote: `address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience` must match the `Scope` that ins-backend requests once `/.default` is stripped, `api://` prefix included. The gateway in dev rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.

claims.statement: The local profile does not change the address lookup simulator's settings, so a locally run stub expects the same default audience.
claims.note: The local profile overrides only the STS issuer among the simulators; it has no address-lookup-simulator block.

claims.statement: The class Javadoc says find and the truncation and find fixtures are a later iteration, though the controller now handles find and two free-text fixtures; no truncation fixture exists.
claims.quote: Only the fixtures iteration 1 needs are wired here; {@code find} and the truncation/find fixtures are iteration 2.
claims.note: The Javadoc is stale against the code below it on find. A truncation fixture (more results than a page holds) is named but not built.

claims.statement: The simulator has no fixture that returns more than three addresses, an address outside England, a Welsh-language address or a paged result; it takes no parameter other than postcode and find.
claims.note: Looked at every case of the switch and both fixtures. The Javadoc names truncation fixtures as not built.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldReturnThreeFixtureAddresses_forTheDefaultPostcode proves postcode SW1A 1AA with a valid bearer answers 200 JSON with totalResults "3" and contains DOWNING STREET.
Test addresses_shouldReturnAddressesShapedLikeTheRealApi proves the SW1A 1AA answer has subBuildingName BUCKINGHAM PALACE, country ENGLAND, match "1" as a string, and no county anywhere.

Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsTheBareGuidRatherThanTheApiUri proves a bearer whose audience is the bare GUID answers 401 with the gateway's exact body and no WWW-Authenticate header.
claims.note: The test comment says this is the exact mismatch the spike hit in dev, and that the missing header is why Spring's authorization failure handler cannot evict a stale token.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldServeTheReservedFreeTextTerms_soFindCanBeDemonstrated proves find=Buckingham Palace answers 200 containing BUCKINGHAM PALACE.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved proves find=Buckingham answers 200 with totalResults "0".
Test addresses_shouldReturn400_whenNeitherPostcodeNorFindIsGiven proves a request with a valid bearer and no search term answers 400 containing "Either postcode or find is required".
Test addresses_shouldReturn204_forTheReservedNoResultsPostcode proves postcode ZZ1 1ZZ answers 204.
Test addresses_shouldReturnARejectedPostcode400_forTheReservedInvalidPostcode proves postcode QQ1 1QQ answers 400 containing "Requested postcode".
Test addresses_shouldReturn503_forTheReservedThrottledPostcode proves postcode XX1 1XX answers 503.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNonJsonHtml_forTheReservedProxyErrorPostcode proves postcode YY1 1YY answers 200 with an HTML content type.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenNoBearerPresent proves a search with no Authorization header answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsWrong proves a bearer with audience api://SomethingElse answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerHasExpired proves a bearer that expired 60 seconds ago answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerSignatureIsWrong proves a bearer signed by a different key, with the right audience and a future expiry, answers 401.
No test covers the 15-second delayed search term TT1 1TT, the free-text term Downing Street, or a request that gives both postcode and find.
claims.note: Walked all 14 tests; none uses TT1 1TT, Downing Street as a term, or both parameters.
